title: U.S. House · New York's 1st Congressional District
area: Eastern Long Island, covering all of Suffolk County east of Smithtown/Islip (the North and South Forks, the Hamptons, and the Suffolk suburbs including Amityville and Babylon).

context.text: Incumbent Nicholas LaLota advanced without a primary after the Republican and Conservative Party primaries were canceled. Christopher Gallant won the June 23, 2026 Democratic primary over Lukas Ventouras, 62.9% to 37.0%. As of September 22, 2026, Cook Political Report and Inside Elections rated the general election "Solid Republican," Decision Desk rated it "Lean Republican," and Sabato's Crystal Ball rated it "Likely Republican."
Two independent candidates, Jordan Maggio and Thomas Sorensen, withdrew or were disqualified and are not on the November ballot.

priorities.text: Describes his focus as border security and opposing New York's sanctuary-city policies, restoring the SALT deduction, and reducing federal spending while protecting Social Security, Medicare, and veterans' health care.
Cites membership in the bipartisan Problem Solvers Caucus and For Country Caucus as reflecting a preference for cross-party solutions over partisanship.

positions.summary: In a January 2026 statement he said he voted to extend the enhanced ACA premium tax credits for three years, while calling the ACA deeply flawed and wanting income caps reinstated.
positions.quote: While the ACA is deeply flawed, I voted to extend the Enhanced Premium Tax Credits for three years to help the nearly 50,000 constituents who rely on them

record.text: Serves on the House Appropriations Committee (Vice Chair, Financial Services and General Government Subcommittee) and the House Small Business Committee (Chairman, Contracting and Infrastructure Subcommittee) in the 119th Congress (2025-2026).
Served on the House Homeland Security Committee and House Armed Services Committee in the 118th Congress (2023-2024).

priorities.text: Says his campaign focuses on affordability (housing, groceries, energy), protecting Medicare, Social Security, and veterans' benefits, and defending voting rights and reproductive freedom.
priorities.quote: Tackle affordability, from housing to groceries to energy, so Long Island families can build stable, secure lives without being priced out of the communities they love.

priorities.text: Says his priorities include affordable housing, education, health care access, fair wages, veterans' benefits, and government accountability.

positions.summary: Says he will fight to protect reproductive freedom.
positions.quote: I'll fight to protect voting rights, reproductive freedom, and the rule of law

positions.summary: Campaign site's health care plan lists expanding Medicare to cover dental, hearing and vision care.
positions.quote: Expand Medicare to cover dental, hearing, and vision care.

statements.quote: Secure federal housing grants to increase workforce housing, starter homes, and attainable housing options for young professionals, first responders, teachers, nurses, veterans, and working families.
statements.context: On his campaign site (Mission One action plan)

statements.quote: Push for affordable childcare tax incentives so parents are not forced to choose between their careers and caring for their children.
statements.context: On his campaign site (Mission One action plan)

researchNotes: LaLota's priorities and positions draw on his 2024 Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey (he had not completed a 2026 survey as of research date); his committee assignments and biography are current. Sponsored-bill detail for LaLota is limited to what Ballotpedia's biography and survey summarize, since congress.gov blocked automated access during research. Christopher Gallant: campaign 'Mission Plan' pages (gallantny.com) were loaded; added a health care position and housing and child care statements. The site does not address guns, immigration enforcement, taxes on high earners or the other listed issues. LaLota's priorities and positions draw on his 2024 Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey (he had not completed a 2026 survey as of research date); his committee assignments and biography are current (the biography draws on his official House biography and Ballotpedia). Gallant's campaign website could not be loaded, so his biography relies on his Ballotpedia survey, VoteVets, and local news; sources differ on when he joined the National Guard, so no start year is given.
